name: Greed-armed trend continuation (persistent risk-on sentiment regime ARMS momentum; gate, not contrarian)
rationale: Plain crypto momentum is exhausted because breakouts fire identically in chop and in real regimes. The Extremity Premium study (arXiv 2602.07018 / rs-8802783) documents that extreme-greed is HIGHLY PERSISTENT (80.2% daily persistence vs 60.3% for neutral) and that sentiment extremity predicts excess uncertainty BEYOND realized volatility — i.e. the regime carries information orthogonal to a vol-only filter. So momentum should be tradable ONLY while the crowd-sentiment regime is risk-on AND persistent; in neutral/fear regimes the same breakout is noise. This is a regime GATE on trend (the inverse of the tired buy-fear contrarian), not a level-in-disguise: entry requires (a) greed NOW (fear_greed >= greed_floor), (b) PERSISTENT greed — fear_greed read persist_lookback days back was still >= persist_floor, so we ride a multi-day regime not a one-day blip, (c) confirmed trend (ret_Nd > mom_floor over a fitted lookback), and (d) a real trend not chop (adx > adx_floor). DISCONFIRMERS (pre-registered): run the SAME momentum entry (ret_Nd>mom_floor + adx floor) with NO sentiment gate, and separately gated by a NON-CAUSAL control (astro_lunar_phase) instead of fear_greed. If ungated momentum OR astro-gated momentum matches the greed-gated net-of-fee Sharpe, the gate adds nothing and this is disguised momentum — falsified. The greed gate must add incremental net edge over plain momentum AND beat the astro control. Because the greed regime is ~80% persistent, the position is held across many days and only flips on a genuine regime transition, keeping taker churn well under the 10bps drag (low turnover). Hedge funds ignore this because the alpha lives in low-capacity spot majors at swing horizon, beneath their cost/capacity floor, and F&G is an un-quantified retail gauge they dismiss as noise rather than mine as a regime tag.
catalyst: momentum continuation while the crowd-sentiment regime is risk-on and persistent
